rich_blocks.narrativeGuidance: Use it when the visitor would benefit from composing their own perspective or seeing how other people have interpreted Henry’s archive. Explain that a View is a dated slice shaped around one angle and grounded in original site material. Keep this focused on creating and exploring Views, while the three-path systems component explains the underlying mechanism.

rich_blocks.title: Insurance configuration rule engine
rich_blocks.description: Try the packing-rule analogue that mirrors the HSBC product-to-UI mapping engine.
rich_blocks.componentDescription: A working analogue of Henry’s HSBC insurance configuration engine. The demo substitutes a trip specification for an insurance product specification, rule columns for business scenarios, and packing items for UI components, then uses the same decision-table logic to map inputs to outputs.
rich_blocks.narrativeGuidance: Use it when the HSBC project, product configuration, mapping, or decision tables are directly relevant. First explain the real mapping from product specification through business scenarios to UI-component requirements. Then explain the trip-and-packing analogy before inviting the visitor to change the inputs.

rich_blocks.title: Cross-page reference linking demo
rich_blocks.description: Connect a cross-page note to the sentence it qualifies and see the resulting retrieval chunk.
rich_blocks.componentDescription: An interactive demonstration from Henry’s PwC RAG ingestion project. It shows how a cross-page note is reattached before chunking and why the resulting retrieval unit contains both the rule and the qualification needed to interpret it.
rich_blocks.narrativeGuidance: Use it when RAG ingestion, cross-page references, chunking, retrieval, or document structure matter to the answer. Explain the structural failure before linking, the ingestion repair, and what changes in the retrieved chunk afterward.

rich_blocks.title: The knowledge behind a question-answering assistant
rich_blocks.description: Explore knowledge gaps, review the research they guide, and monitor the original sources behind accepted knowledge.
rich_blocks.componentDescription: An interactive knowledge workspace supporting the RAG question-answering assistant in Henry’s PwC AI for IT Operations project. A fixed two-by-two matrix crosses known and latent needs with covered and missing knowledge. Its four cases show answering a known question, acquiring knowledge for a real gap, applying existing knowledge to an unasked question, and using AI to predict a valuable uncovered question. The two missing-knowledge cases guide one research objective. Visitors see why the discovered sources contribute useful evidence, with clustering, focused crawling, and re-seeding explained in expandable research notes. Source monitoring revisits the original URLs, compares current content with accepted snapshots, and brings a proposed update to human review only after agent assessment.
rich_blocks.narrativeGuidance: Explain Knowledge Management as the acquisition and maintenance of evidence for the platform’s RAG question-answering assistant. Invite readers to explore the research behind an unanswered question or run a check on an original source. The monitoring workflow compares source content and prepares a knowledge update when needed. Browser Control is a separate capability in the same platform.

rich_blocks.title: An agent handles a workspace-access ticket
rich_blocks.description: Hand a natural-language ticket to AI and follow its work in a separate application tab.
rich_blocks.componentDescription: An interactive service desk dashboard, separate application tab, and floating browser-extension card from Henry’s PwC Browser Control work. Each ticket opens the application immediately. Visitors watch the agent translate the request into actions, pause, take over and edit, or approve the prepared change. The tickets also include a laptop request and an application sign-in. Resolved tickets retain the full action and decision history in the dashboard until the page is refreshed. The extension connects cloud reasoning to the operator’s existing browser.
rich_blocks.narrativeGuidance: A high-priority hands-on example for Views about AI engineering, enterprise automation, or human control of agents. Readers can follow an access ticket from a service desk into a separate application, watch the agent fill the form, then pause, take over, or approve the change. It makes the division between cloud reasoning, browser actions, and operator decisions visible. Introduce the ticket and invite the reader to try an intervention before explaining what it shows. Use only when these actions help answer the reader’s question.

rich_blocks.title: Flowchart reconstruction demo
rich_blocks.description: Compare a source flowchart with its reconstructed Mermaid representation and structured source.
rich_blocks.componentDescription: An interactive comparison from the PwC RAG ingestion project that places the original flowchart beside its Mermaid reconstruction and the structured Mermaid source used for text-based retrieval.
rich_blocks.narrativeGuidance: Use it when VLM-based document understanding, Mermaid, flowchart reconstruction, or diagram retrieval matters. Explain that the reconstruction preserves nodes, edges, labels, and branch structure in a representation that can be searched as text.

rich_blocks.title: Charts and the scenes that create them
rich_blocks.description: Switch between figure types to see a scene schema and its rendered D3 result together.
rich_blocks.componentDescription: A working explorer from Henry’s schema-driven scrollytelling engine. Visitors can switch figure types and inspect the small scene schema beside the output produced by the corresponding reusable D3 renderer.
rich_blocks.narrativeGuidance: Establish that Henry built a scrolling web presentation whose figures appear alongside the explanation. Use this explorer to show how the same chart builders can serve another story with different text and data, then explain the relationship between a scene schema, the renderer registry, and the displayed figure when relevant.

rich_blocks.narrativeGuidance: Use it when experiencing the finished storytelling system adds evidence beyond a technical description. Explain what the sequence demonstrates about the engine.
